problem: The new feed checks cannot fail. When a species has no feed.glb, CreatureClips (scripts/creatures/creature_clips.gd:180-181) adds a copy of idle under the name feed, so the feed state always exists and `pb.get_current_node() == &"feed"` always passes. To prove it, I ran this branch's t_canim.gd against the base tree, where zebraceratops has no feed.glb. Output: "[t_canim] ok   zebraceratops play_clip(feed): state machine on feed" (logs/t_canim_new_on_base.log). Only the sleep half catches a regression there ("FAIL zebraceratops play_clip(sleep): state machine on idle"). The comment says the check covers the 'authored sleep/feed clips', but it does not.
fix: Assert that the feed animation is the authored one, not the idle copy. For example, sample a Head or Neck rotation track at 50% of feed and of idle, and require that they differ by more than a small epsilon. Comparing lengths will not work: zebraceratops feed and idle are both 2.54 s. Then confirm the check fails on the base tree.

problem: The new belly-down sleep is grounded, which fixes the old pose. In-game the lowest bone moved from 0.80 m to 0.00 m and the top from 3.68 m to 2.33 m (bones.gd probe). But the pose has an obvious anatomy defect, visible from gameplay angles in both renderers. A hind foot sits on top of the hip with its toe claws pointing up (after_rex_fwd.png, after_rex_gl.png, after_rexside_fwd.png, after_canimlab_gl.png). A pale, flat wedge of belly skin with straight edges sticks out under the chest (after_rex_fwd.png, around x 420-600, y 520-600). From a camera 0.6 m off the ground, sky shows under the hip span (after_rexbelly_fwd.png). ARK's sleeping rex tucks its legs under the body. The integrator accepted it knowing about the defect.
fix: Re-run trex-sleep with the metatarsals laid flat along the ground and the toes pointing forward, keeping the feet beside or under the thighs. Close the chest skin wedge. Re-vet from a 3/4 camera before merging. If the owner wants the interim clip anyway, record that sign-off in STATUS.
